Base directory for this skill: D:\code\invesments\master_investments_mmo\.claude\skills\ck-plan # Planning Create detailed technical implementation plans through research, codebase analysis, solution design, and comprehensive documentation. ## Prerequisites - **ClaudeKit CLI required:** This skill requires `ck` CLI for plan operations. Run `npm install -g claudekit` if not installed. ## CLI Integration This skill orchestrates planning, but ClaudeKit CLI now owns the plan file scaffolding and phase state mutations whenever `ck` is available. Use these commands instead of hand-editing CLI-managed plan structure: ```bash ck plan create \ --title "{plan title}" \ --phases "{Research},{Implement},{Test}" \ --dir {plan-dir} \ --source skill ck plan create \ --global \ --title "{plan title}" \ --phases "{Research},{Implement},{Test}" \ --dir {plan-dir} \ --source skill cd /absolute/path/to/plan-dir && ck plan check --start cd /absolute/path/to/plan-dir && ck plan check cd /absolute/path/to/plan-dir && ck plan uncheck ck plan status /absolute/path/to/plan.md ck config ui --port 3456 ``` Rules: - Use `ck plan create` to scaffold `plan.md` and `phase-*.md` when the CLI is available. - Default scope is project-local (`./plans/` under the current project). - Global scope is conditional: use `ck plan create --global ...` or fall back to global scope only when no project context exists. - Use `ck plan check` / `ck plan uncheck` for phase status changes. - Do not hand-edit the phases table for status toggles or structural updates when CLI commands are available. - Use the dashboard at `http://localhost:3456/plans` for visual plan management. - **Overwriting phase stub files:** `ck plan create` scaffolds small boilerplate `phase-XX-*.md` stubs. Always **Read the stub before Write** — Claude Code enforces Read-before-Write on existing files; skipping the Read causes the Write to be rejected, wasting the Write's input tokens AND forcing a retry. The stubs are tiny (~15 lines), so the Read cost is trivial. Then Write the full content following the canonical template below. ### Canonical Phase File Template Use this structure when filling each `phase-XX-*.md`. Loaded once with the skill — no per-file Read needed to learn it. Frontmatter fields match the CLI's phase schema; section headers match `documentation-management.md` so phase files stay consistent across plans. ````markdown --- phase: title: "" status: pending # pending | in-progress | completed priority: P2 # P1 | P2 | P3 effort: "" # e.g. "4h", "2d" dependencies: [] # phase IDs this blocks on --- # Phase : ## Overview <1-2 sentences describing what this phase delivers> ## Requirements - Functional: ... - Non-functional: ... ## Architecture ## Related Code Files - Create: `path/...` - Modify: `path/...` - Delete: `path/...` ## Implementation Steps 1. ... 2. ... ## Success Criteria - [ ] ... ## Risk Assessment ```` **IMPORTANT:** Before you start, scan unfinished plans in the active scope first: - Project scope: `./plans/` - Global scope: the configured global plans root - Default when unset: `~/.claude/plans/` If there are relevant plans overlapping your upcoming plan, update them as well. If you're unsure or need more clarifications, use `AskUserQuestion` tool to ask the user. ### Scope Selection - **Project scope** is the default whenever the current working tree has project context. - **Global scope** is allowed only when: - the user explicitly asks for it via `--global`, or - there is no project context to anchor a local plan. - **No project context** means no `.git`, `package.json`, or `CLAUDE.md` was found in the ancestor chain. - Keep scope honest in prose and examples: the skill describes CLI-owned behavior, it does not implement scope resolution itself. ### Cross-Plan Dependency Detection During the pre-creation scan, detect and mark blocking relationships between plans: 1. **Scan** — Read `plan.md` frontmatter of each unfinished plan (status != `completed`/`cancelled`) 2. **Compare scope** — Check overlapping files, shared dependencies, same feature area 3. **Classify relationship:** - New plan needs output of existing plan → new plan `blockedBy: [existing-plan-dir]` - New plan changes something existing plan depends on → existing plan `blockedBy: [new-plan-dir]`, new plan `blocks: [existing-plan-dir]` - Cross-scope dependency → use `global:` or `project:` prefixes - Mutual dependency → both plans reference each other in `blockedBy`/`blocks` 4. **Bidirectional update** — When relationship detected, update BOTH `plan.md` files' frontmatter 5. **Ambiguous?** → Use `AskUserQuestion` with header "Plan Dependency", present detected overlap, ask user to confirm relationship type (blocks/blockedBy/none) **Frontmatter fields**: ```yaml blockedBy: [260301-1200-auth-system] # Same-scope dependency blockedBy: [global:260301-1200-auth-system] # Cross-scope dependency blocks: [project:260228-0900-user-dashboard] # Explicit project-scope dependency ``` **Status interaction:** `ck plan status` is the authoritative inspection surface. Same-scope bare refs stay in the current scope; prefixed refs resolve against the explicit project/global root. Missing refs should warn and show `not found`, not hard-fail the plan. ## Default (No Arguments) If invoked with a task description, proceed with planning workflow. If invoked WITHOUT arguments or with unclear intent, use `AskUserQuestion` to present available operations: | Operation | Description | |-----------|-------------| | `(default)` | Create implementation plan for a task | | `archive` | Write journal entry & archive plans | | `red-team` | Adversarial plan review | | `validate` | Critical questions interview | Present as options via `AskUserQuestion` with header "Planning Operation", question "What would you like to do?". ## Workflow Modes Default: auto-detect planning mode (analyze task complexity and pick mode). | Flag | Mode | Research | Red Team | Validation | Cook Flag | |------|------|----------|----------|------------|-----------| | `--auto` | Auto-detect | Follows mode | Follows mode | Follows mode | Follows mode | | `--fast` | Fast | Skip | Skip | Skip | (none) | | `--hard` | Hard | 2 researchers | Yes | Optional | (none) | | `--deep` | Deep | 2-3 researchers + per-phase scout | Yes | Yes | (none) | | `--parallel` | Parallel | 2 researchers | Yes | Optional | `--parallel` | | `--two` | Two approaches | 2+ researchers | After selection | After selection | (none) | **Composable flags** (combine with any mode): | Flag | Effect | |------|--------| | `--tdd` | Add tests-first structure to each phase for regression-safe refactors | | `--no-tasks` | Skip task hydration | Load: `references/workflow-modes.md` for auto-detection logic, per-mode workflows, context reminders. ## When to Use - Planning new feature implementations - Architecting system designs - Evaluating technical approaches - Creating implementation roadmaps - Breaking down complex requirements ## Core Responsibilities & Rules Always honoring **YAGNI**, **KISS**, and **DRY** principles. **Be honest, be brutal, straight to the point, and be concise.** ### 0. Scope Challenge Load: `references/scope-challenge.md` **Skip if:** `--fast` mode or trivial task (single file fix, <20 word description) ### 1. Research & Analysis Load: `references/research-phase.md` **Skip if:** Fast mode or provided with researcher reports ### 2. Codebase Understanding Load: `references/codebase-understanding.md` **Skip if:** Provided with scout reports ### 3. Solution Design Load: `references/solution-design.md` ### 4. Plan Creation & Organization Load: `references/plan-organization.md` ### 5. Task Breakdown & Output Standards Load: `references/output-standards.md` ## Process Flow (Authoritative) ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Pre-Creation Check] --> B[Cross-Plan Scan] B --> C[Scope Challenge] C --> D[Mode Detection] D -->|fast| E[Skip Research] D -->|hard/deep/parallel/two| F[Spawn Researchers] E --> G[Codebase Analysis] F --> G G --> H[Write Plan via Planner] H --> I{Red Team?} I -->|Yes| J[Red Team Review] I -->|No| K{Validate?} J --> K K -->|Yes| V[Verification Pass] K -->|No| M[Hydrate Tasks] V --> L[Validation Interview] L --> M M --> N[Present Boundary Reminder] N --> P[Post-Plan Handoff
AskUserQuestion: skip gates already auto-run] P --> O[Journal] ``` **This diagram is the authoritative workflow.** Prose sections below provide detail for each node. ## Workflow Process 1. **Pre-Creation Check** → Check Plan Context for active/suggested/none 1b. **Cross-Plan Scan** → Scan unfinished plans, detect `blockedBy`/`blocks` relationships, update both plans 1c. **Scope Challenge** → Run Step 0 scope questions, select mode (see `references/scope-challenge.md`) **Skip if:** `--fast` mode or trivial task 2. **Mode Detection** → Auto-detect or use explicit flag (see `workflow-modes.md`) 3. **Research Phase** → Spawn researchers (skip in fast mode) 4. **Codebase Analysis** → Read docs, scout if needed 5. **Plan Documentation** → Write comprehensive plan via planner subagent 6. **Red Team Review** → Run `/ck:plan red-team {plan-path}` (hard/deep/parallel/two modes) 7. **Post-Plan Validation** → Run `/ck:plan validate {plan-path}` (hard/deep/parallel/two modes) 8. **Hydrate Tasks** → Create Claude Tasks from phases (default on, `--no-tasks` to skip) 9. **Boundary Reminder** → Present optional next-step commands with absolute path 10. **Journal** → Run `/ck:journal` to write a concise technical journal entry upon completion ### Whole-Plan Consistency Gate This gate is mandatory after `/ck:plan validate` or `/ck:plan red-team` edits any plan file. Load: `references/verification-roles.md` → "Whole-Plan Consistency Sweep". Before recommending `/ck:cook`, re-read `plan.md` and every `phase-*.md` file. Search all plan files for stale terms, rejected assumptions, renamed APIs/files/fields, superseded decisions, and duplicate embedded drafts/contracts. Reconcile contradictions across the entire plan, not only the edited phase. If unresolved contradictions remain, report them and ask the user. Do not recommend cook until the whole-plan consistency sweep reports zero unresolved contradictions. ## Output Requirements **IMPORTANT:** Invoke "/ck:project-organization" skill to organize the outputs. - DO NOT implement code - only create plans - Respond with plan file path and summary - Ensure self-contained plans with necessary context - Include code snippets/pseudocode when clarifying - Fully respect the `./docs/development-rules.md` file ## Task Management Plan files = persistent. Tasks = session-scoped. Hydration bridges the gap. **Default:** Auto-hydrate tasks after plan files are written. Skip with `--no-tasks`. **3-Task Rule:** <3 phases → skip task creation. **Fallback:** Task tools (`TaskCreate`/`TaskUpdate`/`TaskGet`/`TaskList`) are CLI-only — unavailable in VSCode extension. If they error, use `TodoWrite` for tracking. Plan files remain the source of truth; hydration is an optimization, not a requirement. Load: `references/task-management.md` for hydration pattern, TaskCreate patterns, cook handoff protocol. ### Hydration Workflow 1. Write plan.md + phase files (persistent layer) 2. TaskCreate per phase with `addBlockedBy` chain (skip if Task tools unavailable) 3. TaskCreate for critical/high-risk steps within phases (skip if Task tools unavailable) 4. Metadata: phase, priority, effort, planDir, phaseFile 5. Cook picks up via TaskList (same session) or re-hydrates (new session) ## Active Plan State Check `## Plan Context` injected by hooks: - **"Plan: {path}"** → Active plan. Ask "Continue? [Y/n]" - **"Suggested: {path}"** → Branch hint only. Ask if activate or create new. - **"Plan: none"** → Create new using `Plan dir:` from `## Naming` After creating plan: `node .claude/scripts/set-active-plan.cjs {plan-dir}` Reports: Active plans → plan-specific path. Suggested → default path. ### Important **DO NOT** create plans or reports in arbitrary user directories. **MUST** create plans or reports in one of these allowed roots: - project scope → current working project directory - global scope → configured global plans root - Default when unset: `~/.claude/plans/` ## Subcommands | Subcommand | Reference | Purpose | |------------|-----------|---------| | `/ck:plan archive` | `references/archive-workflow.md` | Archive plans + write journal entries | | `/ck:plan red-team` | `references/red-team-workflow.md` | Adversarial plan review with hostile reviewers | | `/ck:plan validate` | `references/validate-workflow.md` | Validate plan with critical questions interview | ## Post-Plan Handoff (MANDATORY at session end) After `plan.md` + phase files are written and the user has reviewed/approved them, use `AskUserQuestion` to offer the appropriate next step. Recommend the option that best fits the plan's risk/scope; recommended option listed FIRST and labelled "(Recommended)". | Option | Recommend When | Why | |--------|----------------|-----| | `/ck:plan validate` | Plan is moderate-to-complex; user wants critical-questions interview before implementation | Cheapest gate — surfaces unspecified assumptions, missing acceptance criteria, hand-wavy phases | | `/ck:plan red-team` | Plan touches security, auth, payments, data integrity, public APIs, infra, or has high blast radius | Adversarial reviewers stress-test the plan for failure modes, attack vectors, and missing edge cases | | `/ck:cook ` | Plan is small / well-understood / low-risk and user wants to start implementation | Skip extra gates; go straight to implementation | | End session | User wants to review/share plan before deciding | Stop with plan path returned | **Skip this step ONLY when:** - The current invocation IS already a subcommand (`validate`, `red-team`, `archive`) — those have their own terminal handoff. - User explicitly said "just plan, don't suggest next step". **Skip an individual option ONLY when the active mode already auto-ran that gate (per Workflow Process Steps 6-7):** - Omit `/ck:plan red-team` from the offered options when mode is `--hard`, `--deep`, `--parallel`, or `--two` (Step 6 already ran adversarial review). - Omit `/ck:plan validate` from the offered options when mode is `--deep` (Step 7 already ran validation). - If both gates already ran, the Post-Plan Handoff still fires but offers only `/ck:cook ` and `End session`. After selection: invoke the chosen command with the plan path as argument for continuity. ## Quality Standards - Thorough and specific, consider long-term maintainability - Research thoroughly when uncertain - Address security and performance concerns - Detailed enough for junior developers - Validate against existing codebase patterns **Remember:** Plan quality determines implementation success. Be comprehensive and consider all solution aspects. ## Workflow Position **Typically follows:** `/ck:brainstorm` (after exploring options), `/ck:scout` (after codebase discovery) **May precede:** `/ck:cook` after user approval (otherwise stop with plan path and next-step options) **Related:** `/ck:brainstorm` (explore before planning), `/ck:cook` (execute after planning) ARGUMENTS: plans/reports/brainstorm-260517-stage2-universal-audit-completion-engine.md

```json
        {"id": "anti_confirmation", "rule": "contains('fail|risk|concern|against') OR not_product_analysis()"}
      ]
    },
    "actionability": {
      "weight": 0.2,
      "checks": [
        {"id": "specific_next_steps", "rule": "contains('next step|TODO|action item|will')"},
        {"id": "concrete_not_vague", "rule": "vague_phrase_count('consider|perhaps|might want') <= 3"}
      ]
    }

```

---

## Relationship: System 1 ↔ System 2

```
System 1 (Stage0, brainstorm, think, etc.)
    │ produces output
    ▼
System 2 (Audit hook)
    │ finds gaps
    ▼
System 1 (same LLM, same session)
    │ fills gaps based on injection
    ▼
System 2 (re-audit)
    │ ...loop...
    ▼
FINAL OUTPUT (quality-assured)
```

Key relationship properties:
- **Tight coupling**: System 2 KNOWS System 1's internals (schemas match command specs)
- **Unidirectional control**: System 2 drives System 1, never reverse
- **Same session**: No cross-session state needed (audit history is per-session)
- **Complementary**: System 1 produces, System 2 ensures quality. Neither replaces the other.
- **Progressive**: System 2 schemas can be tightened over time as System 1 improves

---

## Success Metrics

| Metric | Before | Target |
|--------|--------|--------|
| Average output quality (manual score) | 6-7/10 | 8.5+/10 |
| Gaps found post-delivery by user | 3-5 per output | <1 per output |
| Stage0 agent coverage | Often <8 (hook blocks) | Always 8+ (auto-fixed) |
| Unsourced claims in final output | 5-10 per analysis | 0-2 (all tagged [?]) |
| User re-ask rate ("but what about X?") | High | Near-zero |

---

## Risks & Mitigations

| Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
|------|----------|-----------|
| Infinite loop (gap never fills) | High | Convergence detector: stagnation + max_iter |
| False positives (valid output blocked) | Medium | Start with conservative schemas, tighten iteratively |
| Token waste (unnecessary iterations) | Medium | Minor gaps don't block; only critical/major trigger loop |
| Hook performance (slow audit) | Low | All checks are regex/string ops, no LLM calls in hook |
| Schema maintenance burden | Low | Start with 3 schemas (stage0, brainstorm, default), add as needed |

---

## Implementation Approach

Phase 1: Core engine + default schema (works on all outputs)
Phase 2: stage0-specific schema (replace existing stage0-post-audit behavior)
Phase 3: brainstorm + think schemas
Phase 4: code + plan schemas
Phase 5: Convergence tuning from real usage data

---

## Non-Goals (Out of Scope)

- Does NOT replace existing evolution system (meta-evolution, strategy evolution)
- Does NOT generate new content — only audits and requests completion
- Does NOT cross sessions — audit state is per-session only
- Does NOT require new Python infrastructure — pure JS/CJS in hooks
- Does NOT slow down simple queries (quick detection: if output < 500 chars → skip audit)

# Stage 2: Universal Audit-Completion Engine

## Overview

A `Stop` hook (`stage2-audit-completion.cjs`) that fires after every assistant turn, detects output type, loads matching audit schema, runs D1-D7 dimension checks, and either passes (exit 0) or blocks with structured gap injection (exit 2) to drive self-correction loops. Convergence safety prevents infinite loops.

**Source:** `plans/reports/brainstorm-260517-stage2-universal-audit-completion-engine.md`

## Key Decisions

- Pure CJS (no Python, no LLM calls in hook) — regex/string ops only
- Per-session audit history (no cross-session state)
- Only critical/major gaps block; minors tagged [RESIDUAL] and passed
- Convergence: max 5 iterations, stagnation detection, repeat gap marking
- Runs LAST after existing hooks (research-output-validator, stage0-post-audit)

# Phase 1: Core Engine + Default Schema

## Overview

Build the main Stop hook entry point, audit engine library, gap classifier, convergence detector, audit history tracker, and a minimal default schema that works on all output types.

## Requirements

- Functional: Hook fires on every assistant turn, detects output type, loads schema, runs checks, blocks/passes
- Non-functional: <100ms execution (regex only, no LLM calls), no crashes on malformed input

## Architecture

```
stage2-audit-completion.cjs (Stop hook entry)
  → lib/audit-engine.cjs (type detection + schema load + check runner)
  → lib/gap-classifier.cjs (severity scoring)
  → lib/convergence-detector.cjs (stagnation/repeat/max-iter)
  → lib/audit-history.cjs (per-session iteration tracking)
  → lib/audit-schemas/default.json (fallback schema)
```

**Data flow:**
1. Hook receives `assistant_response` from stdin (Claude Code Stop hook protocol)
2. `audit-engine` detects type via trigger patterns
3. Loads matching schema (or default)
4. Runs D1-D7 checks applicable to schema
5. `gap-classifier` scores each failed check
6. `convergence-detector` checks iteration history
7. If actionable gaps + not converged → exit 2 + stderr gap injection
8. If no actionable gaps OR converged → exit 0

## Related Code Files

- Create: `.claude/hooks/stage2-audit-completion.cjs`
- Create: `.claude/hooks/lib/audit-engine.cjs`
- Create: `.claude/hooks/lib/gap-classifier.cjs`
- Create: `.claude/hooks/lib/convergence-detector.cjs`
- Create: `.claude/hooks/lib/audit-history.cjs`
- Create: `.claude/hooks/lib/audit-schemas/default.json`

## Implementation Steps

1. **Create `audit-history.cjs`** — In-memory Map keyed by session. Track: iteration count, gap IDs per iteration, timestamps. Export: `recordIteration(gaps)`, `getHistory()`, `getIterationCount()`.

2. **Create `convergence-detector.cjs`** — Import audit-history. Implement 4 rules:
   - Stagnation: `gaps[n].length >= gaps[n-1].length` for 2 consecutive → force-pass
   - Repeat: same gap_id appears in 2+ iterations → mark `[UNFILLABLE]`, exclude from actionable count
   - Max iterations: count >= 5 → force-pass
   - Only minors: 0 critical + 0 major → pass
   Export: `shouldPass(currentGaps)` returning `{pass: bool, reason: string, unfillable: string[]}`

3. **Create `gap-classifier.cjs`** — Given a list of failed checks (from schema), classify each:
   - `critical`: check has `severity: "critical"` in schema OR matches critical patterns (missing required section, unsourced revenue claim, 0 agents fired)
   - `major`: check has `severity: "major"` OR involves contradictions/missing competitor/unjustified scores
   - `minor`: everything else
   Export: `classifyGaps(failedChecks)` returning `{critical: [], major: [], minor: []}`

4. **Create `audit-engine.cjs`** — Core logic:
   - `detectType(text)`: match against all schema trigger_patterns, return best match or "default"
   - `loadSchema(type)`: require from `./audit-schemas/{type}.json`
   - `runChecks(text, schema)`: for each dimension's checks, evaluate rule against text. Rules are simple string ops: `section_exists(pattern)`, `contains(pattern)`, `count_pattern(pattern)`, `unsourced_number_count()`, `vague_phrase_count(phrases)`, `prose_ratio()`
   - Export: `audit(text)` returning `{type, passed, gaps: {critical, major, minor}, iteration, converged, reason}`

5. **Create `default.json` schema** — Minimal checks applicable to ALL outputs:
   - D1 completeness: output length > 200 chars (skip trivial responses)
   - D5 logic: no "TODO" or "PLACEHOLDER" remaining
   - D6 actionability: contains at least one concrete statement (not all questions)

6. **Create `stage2-audit-completion.cjs`** — Stop hook entry:
   - Read stdin (assistant response text)
   - Skip if output < 500 chars (trivial/conversational)
   - Skip if `isHookEnabled('stage2-audit-completion')` returns false
   - Call `audit(text)`
   - If passed → exit 0
   - If blocked → write gap list to stderr in structured format, exit 2
   - Gap injection format:
     ```
     [STAGE2-AUDIT] Iteration {n}/5 — {critical} critical, {major} major gaps found:
     {gap_id}: {description} — Fix: {fix_instruction}
     ...
     Address these gaps in your response. Say 'skip {gap_id}' for any you cannot fix.
     ```

7. **Write tests** — Unit tests for each module in `.claude/hooks/__tests__/stage2/`:
   - `audit-history.test.cjs`
   - `convergence-detector.test.cjs`
   - `gap-classifier.test.cjs`
   - `audit-engine.test.cjs`

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Hook loads without error on `node stage2-audit-completion.cjs` with mocked stdin
- [ ] Default schema passes trivial responses (<500 chars) without blocking
- [ ] Default schema catches "TODO" / "PLACEHOLDER" in substantive outputs
- [ ] Convergence: max 5 iterations enforced
- [ ] Convergence: stagnation detected after 2 same-or-worse iterations
- [ ] Convergence: repeat gaps marked [UNFILLABLE] and excluded
- [ ] Gap injection format renders cleanly in Claude Code feedback
- [ ] Execution time < 100ms on 5000-char input
- [ ] All unit tests pass

## Risk Assessment

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|-----------|
| False positives on conversational replies | Skip audit for output < 500 chars |
| Hook crash breaks all sessions | Wrap entire hook in try/catch → exit 0 on error |
| Stdin parsing failure | Graceful fallback: if parse fails → exit 0 (fail-open) |

# Phase 2: Stage0 Schema + Integration

## Overview

Create stage0-specific audit schema covering the 11-step pipeline's quality requirements. Integrate with existing `stage0-post-audit.cjs` to avoid duplication — Stage 2 subsumes or extends its checks.

## Requirements

- Functional: Catch stage0 outputs missing failure archaeology, unsourced claims, agent coverage gaps, contradictions
- Non-functional: Compatible with existing stage0-post-audit (either replace or complement)

## Architecture

Stage0 schema checks map to brainstorm D1-D7:
- D1 (Completeness): All required sections present (profile, waves, verdict, execution path)
- D2 (Consistency): No contradictions between agent verdicts
- D3 (Depth): Mechanism explanations, not just scores
- D4 (Evidence): Zone tags on claims, failure archaeology present
- D5 (Logic): Verdict supported by evidence, not arbitrary
- D6 (Actionability): Execution path has specific steps, not vague
- D7 (Domain): Agent coverage >= 8, wave coverage, ground-truth references

## Related Code Files

- Create: `.claude/hooks/lib/audit-schemas/stage0.json`
- Modify: `.claude/hooks/stage2-audit-completion.cjs` (if trigger pattern refinement needed)
- Read: `.claude/hooks/stage0-post-audit.cjs` (understand existing checks to avoid duplication)

## Implementation Steps

1. **Audit existing `stage0-post-audit.cjs`** — Extract all checks it performs. Map each to D1-D7 dimensions. Determine: which checks Stage 2 can absorb vs which remain in the existing hook.

2. **Create `stage0.json` schema:**
   ```json
   {
     "type": "stage0",
     "trigger_patterns": ["/stage0", "## Stage 0", "VERDICT:", "Kill Probability"],
     "dimensions": {
       "completeness": {
         "weight": 0.25,
         "checks": [
           {"id": "s0_profile", "rule": "section_exists('profile|founder|constraints')", "severity": "critical"},
           {"id": "s0_verdict", "rule": "section_exists('verdict|recommendation|GO|KILL')", "severity": "critical"},
           {"id": "s0_execution", "rule": "section_exists('execution|next step|action plan')", "severity": "major"},
           {"id": "s0_risk", "rule": "section_exists('risk|danger|concern|threat')", "severity": "major"}
         ]
       },
       "evidence": {
         "weight": 0.25,
         "checks": [
           {"id": "s0_failure_arch", "rule": "contains('fail|bankrupt|closed|shut down|post-mortem')", "severity": "critical", "fix": "Run failure archaeology WebSearch for this business category"},
           {"id": "s0_zone_tags", "rule": "zone_tag_ratio() >= 0.3", "severity": "major", "fix": "Add [K]/[T]/[?] tags to all factual claims"},
           {"id": "s0_sourced_numbers", "rule": "unsourced_number_count() <= 3", "severity": "major", "fix": "Source or tag [?] remaining unsourced numeric claims"}
         ]
       },
       "depth": {
         "weight": 0.2,
         "checks": [
           {"id": "s0_mechanism", "rule": "contains('because|mechanism|works by|caused by|driven by')", "severity": "major"},
           {"id": "s0_money_flow", "rule": "contains('revenue|margin|cost|pricing|unit economics')", "severity": "major"},
           {"id": "s0_not_surface", "rule": "avg_paragraph_length() >= 3", "severity": "minor"}
         ]
       },
       "consistency": {
         "weight": 0.15,
         "checks": [
           {"id": "s0_no_contradiction", "rule": "no_score_contradiction()", "severity": "critical", "fix": "Reconcile contradicting agent assessments"},
           {"id": "s0_verdict_matches", "rule": "verdict_aligned_with_scores()", "severity": "major"}
         ]
       },
       "domain_specific": {
         "weight": 0.15,
         "checks": [
           {"id": "s0_agent_count", "rule": "count_pattern('persona|agent|analysis by') >= 8", "severity": "critical", "fix": "Fire additional agents to reach minimum 8 coverage"},
           {"id": "s0_anti_confirm", "rule": "contains('against|risk|fail|competition|alternative')", "severity": "major"}
         ]
       }
     },

     "max_iterations": 4
   }
   ```

   - `verdict_aligned_with_scores()`: check verdict direction matches majority of sub-scores
   - `avg_paragraph_length()`: average sentences per paragraph

- [ ] Unsourced claims > 3 → major gap
- [ ] Agent count < 8 → critical gap
- [ ] Contradictions between agents → critical gap
- [ ] Clean stage0 output passes without blocking
- [ ] No conflict with existing stage0-post-audit.cjs

| Over-blocking stage0 (too strict) | Start with critical-only blocking, major as warnings first iteration |

# Phase 1: Core Engine + Default Schema

## Overview

Build the main Stop hook entry point, audit engine library, gap classifier, convergence detector, audit history tracker, and a minimal default schema that works on all output types.

## Requirements

- Functional: Hook fires on every assistant turn, detects output type, loads schema, runs checks, blocks/passes
- Non-functional: <100ms execution (regex only, no LLM calls), no crashes on malformed input

## Architecture

```
stage2-audit-completion.cjs (Stop hook entry)
  → lib/audit-engine.cjs (type detection + schema load + check runner)
  → lib/gap-classifier.cjs (severity scoring)
  → lib/convergence-detector.cjs (stagnation/repeat/max-iter)
  → lib/audit-history.cjs (per-session iteration tracking)
  → lib/audit-schemas/default.json (fallback schema)
```

**Data flow:**
1. Hook receives `assistant_response` from stdin (Claude Code Stop hook protocol)
2. `audit-engine` detects type via trigger patterns
3. Loads matching schema (or default)
4. Runs D1-D7 checks applicable to schema
5. `gap-classifier` scores each failed check
6. `convergence-detector` checks iteration history
7. If actionable gaps + not converged → exit 2 + stderr gap injection
8. If no actionable gaps OR converged → exit 0

## Related Code Files

- Create: `.claude/hooks/stage2-audit-completion.cjs`
- Create: `.claude/hooks/lib/audit-engine.cjs`
- Create: `.claude/hooks/lib/gap-classifier.cjs`
- Create: `.claude/hooks/lib/convergence-detector.cjs`
- Create: `.claude/hooks/lib/audit-history.cjs`
- Create: `.claude/hooks/lib/audit-schemas/default.json`

## Implementation Steps

1. **Create `audit-history.cjs`** — In-memory Map keyed by session. Track: iteration count, gap IDs per iteration, timestamps. Export: `recordIteration(gaps)`, `getHistory()`, `getIterationCount()`.

2. **Create `convergence-detector.cjs`** — Import audit-history. Implement 4 rules:
   - Stagnation: `gaps[n].length >= gaps[n-1].length` for 2 consecutive → force-pass
   - Repeat: same gap_id appears in 2+ iterations → mark `[UNFILLABLE]`, exclude from actionable count
   - Max iterations: count >= 5 → force-pass
   - Only minors: 0 critical + 0 major → pass
   Export: `shouldPass(currentGaps)` returning `{pass: bool, reason: string, unfillable: string[]}`

3. **Create `gap-classifier.cjs`** — Given a list of failed checks (from schema), classify each:
   - `critical`: check has `severity: "critical"` in schema OR matches critical patterns (missing required section, unsourced revenue claim, 0 agents fired)
   - `major`: check has `severity: "major"` OR involves contradictions/missing competitor/unjustified scores
   - `minor`: everything else
   Export: `classifyGaps(failedChecks)` returning `{critical: [], major: [], minor: []}`

4. **Create `audit-engine.cjs`** — Core logic:
   - `detectType(text)`: match against all schema trigger_patterns, return best match or "default"
   - `loadSchema(type)`: require from `./audit-schemas/{type}.json`
   - `runChecks(text, schema)`: for each dimension's checks, evaluate rule against text. Rules are simple string ops: `section_exists(pattern)`, `contains(pattern)`, `count_pattern(pattern)`, `unsourced_number_count()`, `vague_phrase_count(phrases)`, `prose_ratio()`
   - Export: `audit(text)` returning `{type, passed, gaps: {critical, major, minor}, iteration, converged, reason}`

5. **Create `default.json` schema** — Minimal checks applicable to ALL outputs:
   - D1 completeness: output length > 200 chars (skip trivial responses)
   - D5 logic: no "TODO" or "PLACEHOLDER" remaining
   - D6 actionability: contains at least one concrete statement (not all questions)

6. **Create `stage2-audit-completion.cjs`** — Stop hook entry:
   - Read stdin (assistant response text)
   - Skip if output < 500 chars (trivial/conversational)
   - Skip if `isHookEnabled('stage2-audit-completion')` returns false
   - Call `audit(text)`
   - If passed → exit 0
   - If blocked → write gap list to stderr in structured format, exit 2
   - Gap injection format:
     ```
     [STAGE2-AUDIT] Iteration {n}/5 — {critical} critical, {major} major gaps found:
     {gap_id}: {description} — Fix: {fix_instruction}
     ...
     Address these gaps in your response. Say 'skip {gap_id}' for any you cannot fix.
     ```

7. **Write tests** — Unit tests for each module in `.claude/hooks/__tests__/stage2/`:
   - `audit-history.test.cjs`
   - `convergence-detector.test.cjs`
   - `gap-classifier.test.cjs`
   - `audit-engine.test.cjs`

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Hook loads without error on `node stage2-audit-completion.cjs` with mocked stdin
- [ ] Default schema passes trivial responses (<500 chars) without blocking
- [ ] Default schema catches "TODO" / "PLACEHOLDER" in substantive outputs
- [ ] Convergence: max 5 iterations enforced
- [ ] Convergence: stagnation detected after 2 same-or-worse iterations

# Phase 5: Convergence Tuning + Settings Hook

## Overview

Register the hook in `settings.json`, add enable/disable toggle via `ck-config-utils`, tune convergence thresholds based on real outputs, and add observability (iteration count reporting).

## Requirements

- Functional: Hook wired in settings.json Stop event, killswitch via config, iteration metrics
- Non-functional: Zero-downtime activation (can be enabled/disabled without restart)

## Related Code Files

- Modify: `.claude/settings.json` — add Stop hook entry
- Modify: `.claude/hooks/lib/ck-config-utils.cjs` — add `stage2-audit-completion` to known hooks
- Create: `.claude/hooks/__tests__/stage2/integration.test.cjs` — end-to-end test
- Modify: `.claude/hooks/stage2-audit-completion.cjs` — add metrics/logging

## Implementation Steps

1. **Register in `settings.json`:**
   ```json
   "Stop": [
     {
       "matcher": "*",
       "hooks": [
         {
           "type": "command",
           "command": "node \"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\"/.claude/hooks/stage2-audit-completion.cjs",
           "_origin": "stage2-universal-audit-completion-engine"
         }
       ]
     }
   ]
   ```

2. **Add killswitch** in `ck-config-utils.cjs` — ensure `isHookEnabled('stage2-audit-completion')` works. Default: enabled. Can be disabled via `ck config set hooks.stage2-audit-completion.enabled false`.

3. **Add observability** to main hook:
   - Log to stderr (non-blocking): `[STAGE2] type={type} iter={n} gaps={critical}/{major}/{minor} result={pass|block|converged}`
   - On convergence force-pass: `[STAGE2-CONVERGED] reason={reason} unfillable=[{ids}]`

4. **Convergence threshold tuning:**
   - Run hook against 10+ real outputs from recent sessions (manually copy-paste into test fixtures)
   - Adjust thresholds: if >30% false positive rate, loosen checks
   - Document final thresholds in `audit-schemas/_README.md`

5. **Integration test** — Full flow:
   - Mock stdin with a stage0 output missing failure archaeology
   - Verify exit 2 + gap injection on stderr
   - Mock stdin with same output + failure archaeology added
   - Verify exit 0

6. **Create `_README.md`** in audit-schemas/ documenting:
   - How to add new schemas
   - Rule function reference
   - Severity classification guide
   - Convergence behavior

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Hook registered in settings.json Stop event
- [ ] `isHookEnabled('stage2-audit-completion')` returns true by default
- [ ] Disabling via config stops all auditing (exit 0 immediately)
- [ ] Observability logs appear on stderr without affecting output
- [ ] Integration test passes end-to-end
- [ ] False positive rate < 20% on 10 real output samples
- [ ] _README.md documents schema creation process

## Risk Assessment

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|-----------|
| Stop hook not supported in current Claude Code version | Verify hook event name; if "Stop" unsupported, use "PostToolUse" on final tool or fallback to SubagentStop |
| Performance regression (hook adds latency to every turn) | Benchmark: must be < 100ms. Early-exit on short outputs. No file I/O except schema loading (cached after first load) |
| User wants to disable mid-session | Config toggle; also supports `skip` command in gap injection |
